title: Finite exceptional pullback and the normalized cohomological residue map
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, $n\geq1$, $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$, and let $f:Y\to X$ be a finite morphism between Noetherian excellent schemes with $\ell$ invertible [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-exc-excellent-ring]. Use ordinary small-etale $D^+$, costalks $C_zM=R\Gamma_zM$, geometric costalks $C_{\bar z}M$, signed Tate twists, and the normalized immediate residue transition of [def-per-potential-dualizing-complex]. Write $f^!$ for the right adjoint to $Rf_!$ [def-amb-etale-compact-support]. For $z\in Y$, put $w=f(z)$ and $a_z:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(z)\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(w)$ [def-weil-residue-field]. Define the isomorphism
$$B_{f,z,M}:a_z^*C_wM\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Cl}_{a_z}\otimes1}a_z^!\Lambda\otimes^La_z^*C_wM\xrightarrow{T_{a_z}(\Lambda,C_wM)}a_z^!C_wM\xrightarrow{\sim}C_z(f^!M).$$
Here $\operatorname{Cl}_{a_z}$ is the virtual-dimension-zero Gysin map of [lem-per-absolute-gysin-purity], $T$ is the counit-normalized field tensor map of [lem-per-field-exceptional-tensor], and the final arrow is the inverse supported-composition identification of [lem-per-prime-power-supported-calculus]. At geometric points use the induced residue-field identifications.

Suppose $\bar v\rightsquigarrow\bar u$ in $Y$ lies over $\bar y\rightsquigarrow\bar x$ in $X$, both immediate geometric specializations. Lying over means that the maps of geometric points and strict localizations commute [def-weil-geometric-point, def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. For every $M\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ and $q\in\mathbf Z$, one has
$$H^{q+2}(B_{f,\bar u,M}(1))\circ\operatorname{sp}^{q}_{\bar y,\bar x}(M)=\operatorname{sp}^{q}_{\bar v,\bar u}(f^!M)\circ H^q(B_{f,\bar v,M}),$$
where $\operatorname{sp}^{q}$ maps $H^q(C_{\bar y}M)$ to $H^{q+2}(C_{\bar x}M(1))$. No pointwise pinning, dimension function, potentiality, constructibility, or finite Tor amplitude is assumed.

source.place: Expose XVII, Proposition 3.3.1, printed pp.269–270; its vertical arrows are the finite residue-field Gysin comparisons of Proposition 2.4.3.1.
